reason: This text from Ezra 3:1-13 describes the Jewish people's return from Babylonian exile and their rebuilding of the temple altar and foundation. While there is emotional weeping from elders who remember the first temple (v. 12-13), the passage focuses on the leaders' (Jeshua, Zerubbabel, and the priests) organizational and spiritual activities—rebuilding the altar, offering sacrifices, celebrating festivals, and laying the temple foundation. There is no depiction of leaders assigning blame to the people for their suffering or explaining their difficulties as resulting from their own fault. The narrative presents constructive leadership and communal religious restoration, not blame-assignment.
